items.q: A study uses 100 MVA base. What is the base impedance on the 11 kV bus?
items.explain: Zbase = kV^2 / MVA = 121 / 100 = 1.21 ohm; every per-unit impedance on that bus is the ohmic value divided by 1.21.

items.q: A 1000 kVA, 11 kV / 415 V transformer has Z = 5%. Assuming an infinite 11 kV source, roughly what 3-phase fault current does the short-circuit study show on the 415 V bus?
items.explain: Fault MVA = 1000 kVA / 0.05 = 20 MVA, and I = 20e6 / (sqrt3 x 415) = 27.8 kA; 1.39 kA is only the full-load current.

items.q: A 75 kW, 415 V, 3-phase motor runs at pf 0.85 and efficiency 0.90. What full-load current should the feeder be rated for?
items.explain: I = P / (sqrt3 x V x pf x eff) = 75000 / (1.732 x 415 x 0.85 x 0.90) = 136 A; 104 A ignores both pf and efficiency.

items.q: A 415 V 3-phase feeder carries 100 A at unity pf over 200 m of cable with R = 0.2 ohm/km (reactance negligible). What line-to-line voltage drop should the load flow show?
items.explain: Vd = sqrt3 x I x R x L = 1.732 x 100 x 0.2 x 0.2 = 6.9 V; 4 V is the single-conductor IR drop without the sqrt3 factor.

items.q: The load flow report lists a 415 V bus at 0.94 pu. What is the actual bus voltage?
items.explain: Actual voltage = per-unit value x nominal = 0.94 x 415 = 390 V, a 6% drop that most plant specifications flag as under-voltage.

items.q: In a load flow study, the utility grid at 11 kV is modelled as the swing bus. What does that fix, and what comes out of the solution?
options: P and voltage fixed; Q is solved
P and Q fixed; voltage is solved
Voltage magnitude and angle fixed; P and Q are solved
Q and angle fixed; P is solved
items.explain: The swing (slack) bus holds a fixed voltage and reference angle and absorbs whatever real and reactive power is needed to balance the network.

items.q: For a 4 kA fault on an outgoing feeder, the feeder relay operates in 0.25 s. You want a 0.3 s grading margin. What is the minimum operating time to set for the incomer relay at that same fault current?
items.explain: The upstream relay must be slower than the downstream one by the grading margin, so 0.25 + 0.30 = 0.55 s at that current.

items.q: The utility declares a 3-phase fault level of 250 MVA at the 11 kV incoming bus. What fault current should the 11 kV switchgear withstand?
items.explain: I = MVA / (sqrt3 x kV) = 250 / (1.732 x 11) = 13.1 kA; 22.7 kA forgets the sqrt3 for a 3-phase system.

items.q: A transformer nameplate gives Z = 5% on its own 1 MVA rating. Your study base is 10 MVA. What impedance do you enter in per-unit on the study base?
items.explain: Per-unit impedance scales with the MVA base: 0.05 x (10 / 1) = 0.50 pu; the ohmic value is unchanged but the base is ten times larger.

items.q: A cable is rated 200 A at 40 C ambient. At 50 C the derating factor is 0.87 and the grouping factor is 0.80. The load is 150 A. Is the cable adequate?
items.explain: Both factors multiply: 200 x 0.87 x 0.80 = 139 A, which is below 150 A, so the next size up is needed.

items.q: A 415 V panel draws 800 kW at pf 0.80. How much capacitor kVAr is needed to bring the pf to unity?
items.explain: kVA = 800 / 0.8 = 1000, so kVAr = sqrt(1000^2 - 800^2) = 600; unity pf means cancelling all 600 kVAr.
